name: FreeGenVideo
tagline: Create short videos from text prompts or reference images in a browser
description:
FreeGenVideo, also searched as freegenvideo and freegen video, is a browser AI video generator at freegen.video. The homepage, read on November 14, 2026, says it turns a text prompt, or a starting image plus a prompt, into a video, with no sign-up, no login, and no app to install. The generator markup on that page named the model Collart Video General. Aspect ratios in the control were 3:4, 9:16, 2:3, 1:1, 16:9, 3:2, 4:3, and 21:9. Resolution choices were 540P and 720P, with 720P marked selected. Duration was 5 seconds. A switch labeled Generate audio was selected, and its label says it includes generated sound in the video. The page also says available output options depend on the current model, and that you should check the options shown in the generator before you start.

The free allowance on the homepage, and again in the FAQ on the same page, is one video per day. It resets at 00:00 UTC. The FAQ says that when free guest generation is available, you can create from a text prompt or a starting image without registering or logging in. Text to video starts from a written prompt. Image to video starts from an uploaded image plus a prompt. The uploader accepts PNG, JPG, and WebP, up to 5 MB each, and the counter shows 0 of 2 images. The first image is the start frame. A second image can be an end frame, and the control labels that option 540P and 5 seconds. The motion prompt counts to 5,000 characters. Quick-start fills on the page include a room redesign and a sneaker reveal. The homepage says the example clips were generated with Seedance 2.0, and that results vary with the prompt, the reference image, and the model.

The steps on the site are to describe who or what is in the shot, what happens, and how the camera moves, add an image if you want image to video, then preview the result and save it. The page names three uses: a social clip or personal project, a story or animation idea, and a product or ad concept. It says to review the video before publishing. The FAQ says a result will not always match the prompt, and that generated videos are private by default. Prompts, starting images, and the request data needed to run the job are sent to the AI provider for the model in use. Only upload material you have permission to share.

The terms of service, fetched again on November 14, 2026, were last updated 2026-10-22. They say the service is operated by FreeGenVideo and cover accounts, AI generation, credits, subscriptions, and public content. Prices, currency, credit quantities, and billing intervals are shown before checkout. Credits are usage units, not cash. Generation costs are shown before you submit. Stripe processes payment. A return from checkout alone does not establish success. The terms also tell you to protect credentials and API keys, so an account can hold an API key. The homepage fetched the same day did not print an endpoint, a credit price, or an MCP URL. A request for https://freegen.video/pricing returned HTTP 404 and the sentence "This page is not here." The navigation still contains a Pricing link. No dollar amount was on the homepage, the terms, or the privacy policy that day.

The privacy policy, also last updated 2026-10-22 and fetched the same day, says an account can sign in with Google or GitHub. It stores prompts, task status, generated outputs, credit transactions, and service settings, and it processes API key metadata when you use those features. Stripe processes card details. The application does not store full card numbers. For guest generation, ThumbmarkJS computes a fingerprint from browser and device characteristics, and the server stores a keyed hash of that fingerprint to apply device limits. The homepage says the generator runs in a phone, tablet, or computer browser. Footer languages were English, Simplified Chinese, and French.

Best for someone who wants one short clip from a sentence or a photo, without creating an account, and who can wait until the next UTC midnight if that day's video is already used.

Watch out for the limit. One video a day is the published guest allowance, not an unlimited free generator. The controls visible on November 14 were 5 seconds at 540P or 720P. An end-frame image is labeled 540P and 5 seconds, so 720P is not promised for that mode. Example clips are credited to Seedance 2.0 while the generator control said Collart Video General. Prompts and images are sent to the provider. A fingerprint hash is stored for guest limits. The public pricing URL was a 404, so a paid price is not verified from these pages.

Runway, Pika, HeyGen, Revid, StoryShort, Speel, and Motionfly are other video listings here, for a different job. FreeGenVideo is the one in that set that publishes a no-account daily video and does not publish a dollar table on the pages checked November 14, 2026.

Last verified November 14, 2026. People search the brand as freegenvideo. The site writes it FreeGenVideo. The domain is freegen.video.
